text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if there was any specific injury or trauma that preceded it?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury is classic for a specific tendon issue. Can you demonstrate if you are able to fully straighten your right ring finger at the distal joint, or does it remain stuck in a bent position?

text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. To confirm the diagnosis, can you tell me if you feel any tenderness or a gap at the very tip of your finger on the palm side? I will also need to see an X-ray to rule out any associated bone fractures. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Ring_Finger

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of fractures confirms this is a soft tissue injury. Given the mechanism of forced extension, the resting posture of the finger, and the inability to actively flex the distal joint, I am confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
